newsitem.title: USA: Compaq stocks surges on record sales.
newsitem.headline: Compaq stocks surges on record sales.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. posted record fourth-quarter sales Wednesday, pushing its stock higher and raising Wall Street expectations for this year.

Bouyed by the sales growth and forecasts of continued strong personal computer sales this year, executives with the world's largest personal computer maker said they expected to again outpace the industry in 1997.

"If you look at a lot of the market analysts today, they are saying the market should grow around 15 to 20 percent. We believe we will grow ahead of that," said Earl Mason, chief financial officer of the Houston-based company.
Compaq reported profits of $462 million, or $1.64 a share, in the fourth quarter ended Dec. 31, up from $82 million, or 30 cents a share after a charge of 87 cents a share.
Worldwide sales grew 15 percent to $5.4 billion in the fourth quarter, compared with $4.7 billion in fourth-quarter 1995, the company said.

Compaq shares rose $5.25 to $83.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading on the earnings report and news the company opened the books this year with $4 billion in cash on hand to fund sales growth and possible acquisitions.

Compaq shares were moving against the tide, rising in a market that saw the Dow Jones industrial average pulled lower by disappointing earnings that sparked a sell-off in shares of of competitor International Business Machines Corp.

For the full year, Compaq generated $18.1 billion in worldwide sales and $1.3 billion, or $4.66 a share, in earnings. That compared with sales of $14.8 billion and earnings of $789 million, or $2.88 a share, after charges totalling 87 cents a share.
Analysts credited Mason, who was named chief financial officer last May, with trimming inventory levels and investing in the company's sales force to ring up stronger sales.

"This gives the company tremendous flexibility that it never had. When you have a ton of inventory, you are like an oil tanker that can't turn around. Now they are like a small ship," Nomura Research analyst Daniel Ries said.

Josephthal Lyons & Ross brokerage analyst Jay Vleeschhouwer revised his target price to $95 a share for Compaq's common stock and said he expected to boost his estimates of earnings for both 1997 and 1998.
While analysts review their earnings estimates, Compaq plans to revise its own internal targets for finances and inventory turnover, Mason said.
The company cut inventory levels nearly in half to $1.1 billion.

Operating efficiencies were credited with boosting cash on hand from $744.9 million to almost $4 billion over the past year, bankrolling the company's plans to expand its direct sales network and possibly fund acquisitions, he said.
"What we are going to do is use the cash to grow the business," Mason said. Compaq executives plan to meet with analysts Friday to discuss the new asset management plans.
